answer.answer: Straylight is not ready for dependable owner use at 10× corpus growth. The 2026-07-26 current-status note supersedes the older green checkpoint: production-scale retrieval can time out or lose successful results, and ordinary writes copy the full membership manifest. The approved direction is a Markdown-first, changed-files-only architecture with rebuildable derived data and precise checkpoints.

claims.value: The controlling source is `Straylight current status`, updated `2026-07-26T12:00:00-07:00`, because it explicitly supersedes `Projects/Straylight stale checkpoint.md`. The stale checkpoint was recorded `2026-07-23T18:00:00-07:00`; its passing retrieval test corpus and healthy `/ready` result are historical evidence that predates the production-sized timeout and full-manifest-copy findings and must not override the newer note. Current implementation truth says the architecture is not ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth.

At the production-sized owner corpus—about 64,000 active records and 9.6 million estimated source tokens—exact-path reads work, but broad `memory.open` and lexical retrieval are slow and can hit the 30-second database timeout. A successful retrieval lane can also be lost when a later lane fails because the lanes share one transaction. Therefore the older test-corpus pass and healthy `/ready` configuration do not establish dependable production retrieval or owner readiness at 10x corpus growth.

Normal writes copy a full corpus membership manifest. This production-sized full-manifest-copy behavior is the identified write-amplification mechanism and is part of why the current architecture is not ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth; it supersedes the older checkpoint that proposed opening the owner alpha immediately.

The approved simplification is to make current Markdown files the workspace truth; version only changed files; make indexes and derived views rebuildable; checkpoint with exact path, version, and hash references plus changes since a workspace generation; and retain coherent source hydration and compact retrieval packets. This is the approved direction, not a verified completed implementation.
